topic.title: Diffusion Sampling, Consistency, and Stochastic Generation
topic.overview: Diffusion models generate data through a sequence of denoising steps. This topic studies their formulation, training signals, sampling efficiency, and connections to other stochastic processes. Consistency models provide a representative alternative: they learn to map noise toward data directly, supporting one-step generation while allowing additional steps when more computation is available.
topic.whyItMatters: Sampling speed affects whether high-quality generation can serve interactive applications. Understanding which choices govern quality also makes comparisons more useful: a different sampler, representation, or noise schedule can matter as much as a named model family.
topic.evolution: The representatives include denoising diffusion foundations, later consistency and distillation methods, and recent analyses of denoisers and sampling temperatures. Work on image enhancement places diffusion, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck processes, and bridges in a shared stochastic framework, finding task-dependent tradeoffs rather than a universally dominant process.
openQuestions: How can few-step models preserve diversity and controllability?
Which improvements transfer across architectures and tasks under matched training and sampling budgets?
